articles.title: Peyton Manning's Son Marshall Makes HSFB Debut, Watch 2030 QB Complete 1st Pass in Trending Video
articles.summary: The son of an NFL legend made his high school football debut on Thursday.
articles.body:
The son of an NFL legend made his high school football debut on Thursday.

Marshall Manning, the son of Peyton Manning, is a freshman at Baylor School in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and got a few snaps during the second quarter of their season opener against Brentwood Academy.

HS football team snaps 101-game losing streak

Manning, who wears the same No. 16 his father wore at Tennessee, is looking to put together a strong high school career and eventually reach the collegiate level, but it could be a while before he gets regular snaps.

He's currently serving as the backup quarterback to Keegan Croucher, a 4-star senior who is committed to Ole Miss.

Once Croucher leaves in the spring, Manning could have the reins to the Baylor offense as a sophomore.

Manning has the chance to continue the tremendous legacy of his family. His grandfather, Archie, played quarterback at Ole Miss before going on to have an NFL career that featured two Pro Bowl selections.

His father is one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, winning five MVPs, a pair of Super Bowls and countless other accolades before retiring in 2016.

Manning's uncle Eli also had a strong career, winning two Super Bowls and two Super Bowl MVPs. He retired in 2019.

The next generation of the Manning family features not only Marshall, but his cousin Arch, who is coming off a strong first season as Texas' starter and is an early favorite to win the Heisman Trophy and go first overall in next year's NFL draft.

It's safe to say Marshall has plenty of people in his circle who know how to succeed at a high level, but for now, he'll wait his turn as a backup.

articles.title: Rodri, las dudas, el huevo y la gallina
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Sus dudas me hicieron dudar a mí”. Así explicó Mourinho a Pedrerol el caso Rodri, anteanoche presentado entre clamores en el Gamper.  Mi duda es dónde nacieron las dudas. Hemos visto en su día a Florentino arrancar, verano tras verano, a Figo del Barça, a Zidane de la Juve, a Ronaldo del Inter de Milán y a Beckham del Manchester. Y ahora Rodri, que no ocultaba su deseo de venir al Madrid y sólo le quedaba un año en un City tiempos de mudanza, se le ha escapado.  Puede ser que no quisiera pisar la huella de Riquelme, puede ser que no le convenciera el modelo de juego que nace en torno a Rodri, fútbol agrupado y masticado, sin vértigo (recuerden que nada más llegar traspasó a Redondo).  Puede ser, en definitiva, que se viera arrastrado por el ambiente creado tras el Mundial, con Rodri reivindicado por el madridismo como ansiada solución para la media, donde aún se arrastra la nostalgia de Kroos. Y como tampoco el modelo preferido de Mourinho es ese del juego bien armado en la media… En fin, en este caso las dudas remiten al acertijo eterno sobre qué fue antes, si el huevo o la gallina. Pero, con todo y eso, el Madrid ha hecho un buen mercado, conservando lo mejor (la renovación de Vinicius no se daba por segura), mejorando puntos débiles de la defensa, trayendo a Bernardo Silva, un artesano de la media, y apostando por el joven Diomande que, precio aparte, suscita grandes esperanzas.  Desde luego, Florentino ha cuidado a Mourinho mucho mejor que hace un año a Xabi Alonso. Por lo que vamos viendo, este Madrid se va a configurar en un 4-2-3-1 (dibujo del que Bilardo se reclamó en su día inventor), con cuatro espléndidos lobos arriba para cazar en manada: Diomande, Bellingham, Vinicius y Mbappé, respaldados por buenos repuestos llamados Brahim, Güler, Rodrygo y el joven Espí. Y espero que entre los dos de la media esté, al menos en días difíciles, Bernardo Silva. Con los laterales mejorados, debe ser un buen equipo si Mourinho consigue de sus figuras de arriba una decente aportación defensiva. Empezaremos a verlo mañana, en Cornellà.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Brighton midfielder Lia Walti 'missed feeling of being valued'
articles.summary: Brighton midfielder Lia Walti said she "missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer" and craved a return to the Women's Super League.
articles.body:
Brighton midfielder Lia Walti said she "missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer" and craved a return to the Women's Super League.

The Switzerland captain left Arsenal for Juventus in 2025 but her short time in Italy exposed the stark differences between the WSL and other leagues.

Walti helped former club Arsenal win four major trophies during a seven-year spell there, including the Champions League and WSL titles.

She moved to Italy in search of a new challenge but quickly realised the differences in professionalism were "extreme".

After one season, Walti returned to England, joining ambitious WSL club Brighton last month for an undisclosed fee.

"It's such a huge difference. It's always hard to speak about it. I don't want to speak too negatively about the Italian league, that is not my aim," Walti told BBC Sport.

"It's more that it's just the reality that football in England, in the WSL, has a standard which is not comparable with any other league.

"It's a bit sad and disappointing to see a lot of girls abroad do not have the same opportunities or standards in terms of being in professional environments."

Walti said she realised the WSL's standards "are not the norm" and she missed playing in front of an established football culture.

"I missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer, feeling like we're getting the full support we needed," added Walti.

"We have good structures, good fields where we can play our games. We had absolutely no fan culture - not just at Juve - in general in Italy.

"When you have been part of that growth in England, with the fan cultures, the full stadiums - even stadiums that are really small, they are exciting to play in.

"In Italy, it was just [empty]. Every game felt a bit like that. I missed the feeling I had before when I was playing football."

Why are there so few African players in the WSL?

New-look Villa turn to Scandinavia as they rebuild squad Published 6 days ago

New-look Villa turn to Scandinavia as they rebuild squad

The 33-year-old made 183 appearances for Arsenal and established herself as a key player for the club.

She captained her country at Euro 2025 on home soil and has over a century of appearances for Switzerland.

Walti's experiences have come as part of a generation that has catapulted women's football growth in England and she believes others can follow suit.

"I think you have to bring the game to the people. You kind of have to force people to watch it. I felt that that's how it maybe started in England," said Walti.

"In Italy, and in a lot of other countries, I think they have bad coverage. It's not shown [on TV] at all, or if it's shown, from where they film it, is really poor.

"It affects the way you watch a game. You don't really see the speed, the tactics or anything and you don't enjoy watching the game.

"In England, in the big stadiums, you can have great camera angles. I think people enjoy watching it more."

While the standard of coverage is a key issue according to Walti, she says there are "so many different things" that are also lacking in women's football globally.

"The biggest lacking starts with pitch quality. In a lot of countries, you play either on the worst artificial pitches or the worst natural grasses," added Walti.

"Even if a Premier League team were to play there, it would probably look rubbish because it's just not possible to play nice football on it.

"All of the other leagues, where do you even start? It's so hard. We have the same [issues] in Switzerland.

"You have to do the first step - invest money for all those things before you get something back. I think a lot of countries don't have that money or patience."

Walti said she is "passionate" about pushing for change because she is privileged to have experienced professionalism in England.

"We used to not have good conditions. It wasn't professional. Our first salaries were not enough to live from," said Walti.

"Now, seeing the growth in England and being with players who try to push the game in their own countries, it makes you feel frustrated to still see the reality.

"You forget sometimes, when you're in your own bubble, that this is not the norm. You're just one of the lucky ones who can experience it.

"A lot of talent in women's football gets lost because they are in bad environments where nobody sees them or they don't have the chance to reach their potential.

"I try to make an impact and I think that was really hard in Italy because I felt like when we spoke up, nothing happened, and that was frustrating."

When Walti was weighing up her future, with a year left on her Juventus contract, she knew Brighton were a club who could offer her a quality environment.

In April, Brighton released their plans for Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium, which will cost £75-80m.

In 2021, the women's team moved into their training facilities at the American Express Elite Football Performance Centre - the result of an £8.5m investment.

On the pitch, they have invested during the transfer window and reached the Women's FA Cup final for the first time in May.

Dario Vidosic's side have ambitions of breaking into the WSL's top three and Walti believes she has joined a club "that cares" about women's football.

"After that experience in Italy, I knew a bit more about what I probably wanted, or didn't want," said Walti.

"I had a pretty big trust in Brighton before we had the conversations because I had been in the league and seen what the club was doing.

"I've heard from other players about the club investing a lot and I only heard really positive things. There is no better feedback than from other players.

"Once I started to have the first moments with the club, it proved to me that this is the right place - that cares about women's football, that invests in women's football, and who has the right people in place."

articles.title: Mourinho: "Los capitanes están jugando un poco a la defensiva..."
articles.standfirst: El portugués afronta su segunda etapa en el banquillo blanco con un discurso exigente y 42 minutos de comparecencia ante los medios
articles.summary: El portugués afronta su segunda etapa en el banquillo blanco con un discurso exigente y 42 minutos de comparecencia ante los medios
articles.body: José Mourinho ya ha vuelto a sentarse ante los medios como entrenador del Real Madrid y lo ha hecho con una comparecencia larga y cargada de mensajes: 20 preguntas y 42 minutos en su primera rueda de prensa oficial desde su regreso al banquillo blanco. El portugués, que firmó hasta 2029 y afronta su segunda etapa en el club trece años después, ha mostrado una versión más serena pero sin renunciar a su contundencia, insistiendo en la responsabilidad de representar al club blanco, en las exigencias que ha trasladado al vestuario y en la necesidad de recuperar determinados valores competitivos. Su regreso llega además en vísperas del debut liguero ante el Espanyol, después de una pretemporada en la que ha dejado claro que quiere un equipo intenso, comprometido y capaz de asumir su propia evolución futbolística. “Es un buen equipo. Los equipos que tienen el mismo entrenador desde hace tiempo son equipos bien preparados. Juega bien y con ambición. Me gustó mucho su primer partido y ahí están, con tres puntos en la clasificación y con la afición feliz. Estamos preparados para lo que nos vamos a encontrar”. “Yo estoy bien. Es el primer partido oficial de la temporada. Estoy tranquilo. Es una temporada y un partido más. La plantilla tiene una dificultad de empezar en diferentes momentos. Hay gente que tiene 36 entrenamientos y 5 partidos, otros menos. También he podido preparar el trabajo diferenciado para todos. Hubo momentos de un jugador para diez personas… Pero estoy contento con la situación. Si me dices que tengo una semana más para preparar las cosas te digo que sí, pero estamos cansados de amistosos". "Los lesionados de la temporada pasada son lesiones de mucho tiempo y no los espero recuperar en una semana. El único jugador que está fuera de este partido es Endrick, que tiene una pequeña cosa muscular. Tchouameni está bien, está entrenando con el equipo. Tiene que entrenar hoy, mañana y domingo para acelerar su proceso". “Yo no diría presión, diría adrenalina que llega y que es positiva. La quiero y el día que no la siento hay algo que no está bien. Pero no siento presión por el debut y siento confianza por el trabajo que hemos hecho. Tengo mucha confianza en la ambición de los jugadores y en su mentalidad. En la pasión que me están mostrando cada día. Mañana, cuando nos metamos en el avión, estaremos convencidos de que vamos a volver con los tres puntos". “Es una expresión. No vamos a seguirla palabra por palabra. Es una expresión que me gusta. Yo estoy disponible para morir por mi grupo y por el Real Madrid. Cuando utiliza mi nombre creo que quiere relacionarlo con el grupo de trabajo y del club. Muchas veces las palabras son fáciles, pero las palabras de Diomande no son diferentes de lo que yo veo en todos. Veo a la gente muy comprometida y con la voluntad muy grande de hacer las cosas bien. Veo un grupo que crece y que está unido. No somos el grupo perfecto porque eso no existe. No voy a pensar que voy a estar semanas sin tener ningún problema. Pero el mensaje de Diomande es un mensaje que se aplica a todos". “Yo he llegado con mucha información, para decir la verdad. Tengo mis contactos de base y he llegado a saber muchas cosas, pero he decidido partir de cero. Desde el primer día que llega Tchouameni yo estoy atento y no he tenido ninguna necesidad de hablar porque he visto inmediatamente la normalidad. Han sido ellos, Federico (Valverde) y Tchouameni los que me han mostrado que no tengo que hablar con ellos y que no tengo que traer la paz. He visto la normalidad y la paz. Es como si no hubiera pasado nada”. “La noticia no ha sido una sorpresa. Mi primera pregunta era: ‘¿Este se quiere quedar o no?’. En ese momento me he quedado absolutamente tranquilo. No quiero valorar si es uno de los tres mejores o no. Pero los mejores tienen que estar aquí”. “La temporada exitosa hay muchos modos de mirarla. Pero al final, el único modo de ser pragmático son los resultados. Se hace un gran trabajo a muchos niveles, hacer crecer la estructura de un club, preparar el club para los próximos 10 años. Pero al final son los resultados los que cuentan. Tenemos cuatro competiciones. O, si queremos decirlo, tres más una pequeña competición. Pero terminar una temporada del Real Madrid sin trofeos no es una temporada exitosa”. “Mañana estarán tres en el banquillo: Rivas, Cestero y Ciria. Tenemos una plantilla no demasiado larga. Militão, Rodrygo y Ferland (Mendy) estarán fuera por mucho tiempo. A mí me gusta mucho trabajar con 20-21 jugadores, máximo 22. Los canteranos están ocupando estas posiciones libres y trabajando muy bien con nosotros. No serán siempre los mismos. Voy a querer también motivar a los niños y hacerles entender que la puerta está abierta. Esta semana les toca a estos tres y les tocará a muchos más. Es una cosa que me gusta hacer y que pienso que se agradece desde La Fábrica, porque es una cosa que pienso que puede motivar a los chicos”. “Estoy contento con todos. Pienso que los capitanes me están conociendo. Ellos también tienen esta capacidad de observar, analizar y conocer bien. Yo no hablo para hacer que me conozcan a través de mis palabras. Quiero que me conozcan por el modo como me observan y como me analizan. Cada mañana a las ocho tenemos una reunión de staff. Es un staff que estuvo aquí los años anteriores y son ellos mismos los que transmiten la idea de que se ve un grupo con una empatía diferente. Y los capitanes aún no han tenido ese momento de serlo en un momento difícil, que llegará. Cuando llegue el momento difícil veremos, pero de momento hay muy buena cooperación. El grupo también está ayudando mucho a los capitanes a estar en un periodo de observación y de tranquilidad”. “Necesitamos ser un equipo, trabajar bien, y no intentar negociar cosas que son innegociables. El compromiso no tiene modo de no estar cada minuto de cada partido. Tenemos que superar momentos de frustración que van a llegar por un resultado negativo o por una frustración personal. Hablaba con los jugadores que, por primera vez, va a llegar mañana un momento de frustración para muchos, que es el primer partido. Será la primera vez que el entrenador tiene que elegir y uno juega de inicio y le sienta bien. También será la primera vez que uno vaya al banquillo y se sienta frustrado. Estos momentos son los que ellos tienen que saber digerir individualmente y como grupo. Yo estoy aquí para ayudarlos, pero hay una cosa que no puedo hacer, que es empezar un partido con 15 jugadores. Solo puedo empezar con once y espero que cada partido sea un momento difícil para mí. El día que uno se deje comer por la frustración y baje el nivel, las decisiones serán fáciles para mí. Yo no quiero decisiones fáciles, las quiero difíciles. Para llegar al final de la temporada y tener algo que celebrar, un equipo como nosotros tiene que saber pasar momentos de frustración individualmente y como un equipo”. "Es siempre difícil entrar en un nuevo club, es una cosa que me hace mal decir: 'este no va a seguir'. Intento cambiar lo menos posible y siempre vengo con gente que me ayude a inculcar una cultura de trabajo. Tenemos siete analistas y sólo he traído uno. A nivel de datos y control del entrenador y el esfuerzo... he traído uno y estoy muy contento de eso. La gente que estaba ha crecido y se ha adaptado. Khedira, en todos los clubes me gusta alguien de la casa. He pensado en jugadores de mi tiempo y de jugadores que ya no juegan, con un perfil psicológico que me guste... ves los nombres. Xabi, entrenador top, Arbeloa igual, Granero businessman (hombre de negocios)... con Khedira me dijo que si tenía que estar mañana, ahí iba a estar. Crece mucho a nivel de campo. El resto de los que estaban conmigo en Benfica son mi gente. Llopis y Nuno ha sido una de las cosas que me ha hecho mal. No conozco su trabajo, quizás ha hecho una cosa que no debería haber hecho... pero yo quería a una persona que ya trabajase conmigo. Por eso he decidido cambiar. Pintus y Silva he pensado que los dos podían encajar muy bien" "No hay un déficit... hubiera sido como la guinda del pastel. Es un gran jugador y con gran experiencia... pero cuando tú tienes Tchouaméni, Valverde, Bernardo o Arda... que podrá jugar en esas posiciones, pues te das cuenta de que no tendremos problemas". "No sé el motivo porque ha tenido algún problema anterior. No lo sé. Lo que veo es que quiere ganar. Sabe lo que quiero yo, sin duda. Pienso que está feliz, que está cómodo por como preparamos los partidos y quiere ganar desde el primer día. Antes de firmar, cada pequeña conversación acababa en "vamos a mejorar, vamos a volver a ganar, a ser felices". Siempre en esta base". "El primer once de Mou... vamos a ver quien de vosotros tiene mejores contactos (risas). Los jugadores saben ya quien juega, mi trabajo no es de esconder. Quizás dentro de un par de horas os llegará la información. No tengo un once ideal o si tengo, no quiero tenerlo. Quiero la puerta abierta a la competición. Son muchos partidos, estaremos en periodos de tres partidos en poco tiempo... y luego 'vacaciones' por el parón de selecciones. Sabemos cómo queremos presionar, compactar, cómo jugar contra un equipo que juega con varios sistemas".

articles.title: Bangladesh expect ‘harder’ Australia challenge in second Test, says coach
articles.summary: After a first Test win in Australia in the series opener, Bangladesh expect a backlash in second match in Mackay.
articles.body:
Bangladesh coach Phil Simmons has warned his players to expect a fierce backlash from Australia in the second Test after his side shocked the cricket world with a nine-wicket victory in the series opener in Darwin.

Australian media dubbed their team’s defeat last weekend as the “Darwin Disaster”, and Simmons said his side could not afford to ⁠be complacent when they face the World Test Championship standings leaders in Mackay, starting Saturday.

“The only thing I had to say to them – and I will repeat it anyway – is that Australia ⁠is going to come harder,” Simmons said on Friday.

“We have to either keep that level of performance or get a little bit better. Even if we have to get 1 percent better in some areas, then we will have to make sure that that’s there.

“But we know that they are going to change their game. ‌They are going to come harder at us.”

The win in Darwin was Bangladesh’s first Test victory on Australian soil and one that Simmons said was among the most satisfying results of his long career coaching red-ball cricket.

The former West Indies all-rounder also hinted he was reluctant to alter a winning combination despite left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam pressing for selection after impressing in training.

Shoriful, who has taken 27 wickets in 13 Tests, missed the first match due to a ⁠hamstring injury.

“He offers something different. But again, we just won a Test ⁠match,” Simmons said.

“I’m one … who hardly likes to change winning teams. So it’s a possibility, but I can’t really say.”

Aussies make one change as Lyon retained and Renshaw comes in

Australia confirmed on Friday they have made just one change to their team for the second Test with Matt Renshaw ⁠coming in at the top of the order for Jake Weatherald, who was dropped on Tuesday after six underwhelming Tests.

Captain Pat Cummins initially told a news conference that Australia were considering bringing in a ⁠fourth paceman in Scott Boland and leaving ⁠out spinner Nathan Lyon, who took 1-125 in Darwin in his first match back after a hamstring injury last December.

But barely an hour later, officials confirmed Lyon was safe after another look at the wicket on the predicted pace-friendly pitch at the Great Barrier Reef Arena.

With the exception of Steve Smith (71 and 44) and second-innings century-maker Cameron Green, the Australian batting was poor in Darwin. Cummins said he was looking for a much-improved performance from the team in Mackay.

“I certainly felt like we didn’t play anywhere near our best, and they played really well and they deserved to win,” Cummins said.

“So, I think it’s going back to when we play well. Fortunately we’ve got a decent body of work to look back on.

“I thought our prep was excellent, so I think everyone’s in a pretty good nick. So it’s just about translating our form into actually a good result,” he added.

articles.title: Mohamed Salah: How Trabzonspor pulled off deal for ex-Liverpool forward
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah was expected to move to Saudi Arabia or the United States after leaving Liverpool, but Turkish side Trabzonspor pulled off one of the coups of the transfer window.
articles.body:
As Mohamed Salah signed his two-year deal in front of tens of thousands of fans inside Trabzonspor's Papara Park stadium, the man putting his signature to the contract next to the Egyptian was struggling to keep the smile off his face.

The reaction of supporters over the previous few days had already convinced club president Ertugrul Dogan he had pulled off a transfer coup.

"He's the biggest Muslim footballer in the world. He's an influential role model," he told BBC Sport Africa and BBC Turkish.

"We held Salah's signing ceremony in front of 35,000 people.

"It was clear from everything he did that he felt that love, and he told us as much too. He thanked us."

So how did Dogan persuade one of football's megastars to join a club without Champions League football and which has won the Turkish title only once since its heyday in the 1970s and early 1980s?

Located on the Black Sea coast, the city of Trabzon sits near the border with Georgia in the north-east corner of Turkey.

With a population of around 800,000 people, it is not even in the top 20 when it comes to the country's largest urban centres.

But Dogan claims it has something special.

"I always say this about Trabzonspor and the city - we're the biggest one-club city in the world.

"Salah asked us something like, 'Why should I choose Trabzonspor now?'

"We told him about the city and said: 'You can be sure you will meet a group of supporters unlike any you have experienced before. You'll feel the genuine love those people have inside them'."

Born in January 1977, Dogan is himself a son of Trabzon.

The businessman made his money through a series of different ventures, including real estate and hazelnuts, before moving into the energy sector and specialising in biofuels.

He became Trabzonspor president in 2023, shortly after the club's most successful season in recent memory - having won the league title in 2021-22.

Under Dogan's watch, the Black Sea Storm, as the club is known, have finished third, seventh and third in the Super Lig.

Last season they won the Turkish Cup under coach Fatih Tekke, who is now looking to guide his team into the Europa League, despite a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg of their play-off tie against Hungary's Ferencvaros.

"We are working to make Trabzonspor and Trabzon itself a destination for talented young players from all over the world," said Dogan.

"We want to take them to the next level, to move on to bigger European clubs. Those young players… [combined with] star players… a star in every way, with their lifestyle, their professionalism, their smile, their positive energy.

"Mohamed Salah is a really great example in this respect."

Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king? Published 5 days ago

Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king?

Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor? Published 6 August

Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor?

Attention 'cannot be given financial value'

During the off-season, Trabzonspor sold 20-year-old Ivorian midfielder Christ Inao Oulai to Fiorentina and Brazilian forward Felipe Augusto, 22, to Zenit St Petersburg - both for large profits after only one season at the club.

Young players from Albania, Belgium, Cape Verde and Portugal have arrived to replace them, but Dogan wants to continue balancing those talents with experienced names.

Cameroon goalkeeper Andre Onana has returned for a second season on loan from Manchester United, but the deal for Salah is the potential gamechanger.

"The attention it has generated and the level of engagement it has created around the world cannot easily be given a direct financial value," explained Dogan, who has openly admitted that Salah will be earning €17m per year (£14.6m, $19.9m), as well as 20% of any merchandise with his name on.

"Purely from a financial perspective, this transfer has no direct return as such.

"We put up our season tickets this year. We had to make another increase. I told our fans, 'Look, I'm bringing you Salah, one of the biggest stars in the world'."

Dogan says nearly 70% of Salah's salary this year was covered by season ticket sales made within the first four or five days after the announcement of his arrival.

The initial target was 25,000 season ticket sales, but the club now expects to exceed 30,000, while major companies have been calling the president, looking to get involved in Salah-mania.

"We're having important discussions in Turkey, Europe and the Arab world as well."

The news that Trabzonspor had won the race for Salah's signature after nine stellar seasons at Liverpool raised a few eyebrows.

Many had expected the man who sits fourth on the all-time list of Premier League goalscorers to sign a huge contract with a club in the Saudi Pro League like Cristiano Ronaldo or join Lionel Messi in the United States.

But while there was competition, Dogan says the deal happened quickly once negotiations really got going.

"Once we started talking, both sides genuinely approached each other very sincerely," he said.

"We'd actually been pursuing him since the World Cup, but we knew at the start he was also talking to other clubs."

This meant Trabzonspor initially had to bide their time, given Dogan says there is an unwritten rule in Turkey that if one club is holding talks then the others will wait.

"Yes, there were clubs in Turkey who were interested," he confirmed.

"After they said, 'We've pulled out of this transfer', we started talks. I think it took about five or six days to conclude.

"We had the first meeting over Zoom. At that point it was really just the two sides getting to know each other. Then Salah was on holiday - he was in Mykonos - and after that the talks continued again via Zoom."

Trabzonspor finally brought Salah to Turkey for his medical in Istanbul.

Dogan says they decided to hold it there to show the 34-year-old the kind of reception he would get across Turkey, not just in Trabzon.

Thousands of fans were at the airport to greet Salah when he arrived, even though it was in the middle of a working day.

Trabzonspor's new star also made his debut in Istanbul, entering the fray as a second-half substitute in a 1-1 draw against Kasimpasa on the opening day of the new league season last weekend.

He is expected to make his home league debut in Trabzon on Sunday.

"The whole city lives for football," said Dogan.

"Everywhere you go, on every corner, the city gives that player that energy and that happiness."

Thanks to Mohamed Salah, Trabzonspor's president could be smiling for a while yet.

articles.title: Expert College Football Betting Locks for 2026 Conference Champions
articles.summary: Despite what the headlines and momentum tell us, it still means something to win a conference in college football. Of course it does.
articles.body:
Despite what the headlines and momentum tell us, it still means something to win a conference in college football. Of course it does.

While the allure and spectacle of the College Football Playoff have cast a shadow on the notion of being the last team standing in the regular season, the journey from fall camp to conference king is still a long and winding road.

For further proof of this, consider that Duke—yes, Duke—won a conference championship in football last season, ending a 63-year drought.

As the season approaches, we're tackling the futures market before making our way into the season. And we're beginning with conference championship betting, a four-month journey that takes us from coast to coast.

There was a case to be made for BYU, especially with the star power at quarterback and receiver. We made cases for Utah and Houston and even looked at the likes of Arizona and Oklahoma State.

Ultimately, we landed with one of the nation's most talented rosters, despite a slew of significant departures and a turbulent offseason. (Perhaps that's putting it mildly.)

Still, the roster is loaded. The offensive line should be exceptional, and the skill talent is deep. The question, of course, comes at quarterback. While the glimpses of Will Hammond were superb, he's coming off a season-ending knee injury and an expedited rehab.

He doesn't have to be Patrick Mahomes—at least not to win the conference. Having an exceptional defense, even without David Bailey and Jacob Rodriguez, will help. This group certainly has a few gaping holes to fill, although there are players at every level capable of filling in.

Then there's the schedule. More than anything, it brings the whole concoction together. To say it's underwhelming would be an understatement. Road games at Cincinnati, Oklahoma State and Baylor are mildly intriguing, but that's being generous.

The path is clearly defined. If the QB is simply "good," Texas Tech should repeat its efforts from a season ago. The value isn't exactly great, but we aren't rushing any other direction.

Typically, a conversation about Oregon football starts with the offense. Well, that or the uniforms.

Since Chip Kelly changed the program, offense has largely told the tale of the Ducks. But of late, with the hire of Dan Lanning, that has started to change. Oregon had the 12th-ranked scoring defense last season; the year before, the Ducks were No. 16.

This year, Dan Lanning's group might wind up being one of the nation's best. It starts with the defensive front, highlighted by A'Mauri Washington, Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti. The back half, however, should be superb as well, highlighted by safety transfer Koi Perich.

Offensively, well, things feel pretty Oregon-y. Dante Moore is back at quarterback, and he is surrounded by a slew of weapons and speed. When you consider how little Moore played prior to last season, it wouldn't be shocking to see his game rapidly evolve.

In short, this team is loaded—and balanced.

The issue is that the Big Ten has a few teams with plenty of firepower. Ohio State, which Oregon plays on the road in early November, will be excellent. Indiana, a team the Ducks won't see in the regular season, has reloaded as well.

The schedule isn't exactly awful; games at USC and home games against Michigan and Washington stand out. But this team—and roster—just seem to be a cut above on all fronts.

Ohio State is the favorite, although Oregon feels positioned to take the Big Ten, even with that road trip on tap.

Let's be blunt: This was the easiest conference champion to pick. It was also the chalkiest.

Sure, Miami lost plenty of talented players. In fact, six players were taken in the first three rounds of the draft this past spring. Despite the losses, one could argue that the Hurricanes could wind up being better, especially on the offensive side.

The addition of quarterback Darian Mensah is enormous. At Duke, Mensah was a difference maker. At Miami, he could be a Heisman winner.

The defense certainly has to fill some large holes, and it wouldn't be shocking to see this group take a step back as the offense takes a leap forward. The schedule and the state of the ACC bring this play into focus.

Florida State is still lost. Clemson continues to regress. Virginia Tech hasn't been right for some time despite showing occasional signs of life. The list goes on.

The only real challengers to Miami appear to be Louisville and SMU. Unfortunately, the Hurricanes won't face either team in the regular season.

The schedule is incredibly manageable, to put it mildly.

Instead, however, this feels more about talent. Miami is a supremely gifted team with an incredibly promising new quarterback.

An encore season seems reasonable. In fact, we should expect it.

A few years ago, the Texas Longhorns were moments away from being fully back. Last year, despite one of the nation's most difficult schedules and an ugly start, they closed the year with tremendous momentum.

If you're a believer in this team—and we clearly are—you're a believer in Arch Manning.

Sure, it was rough for a while last year. The hype was too big, the mechanics were messy and the performance was underwhelming out of the gate. But his play at the end of the year was vastly improved, and the program did everything possible to improve the pieces around him.

The additions of wideout Cam Coleman and running back Hollywood Smothers were massive. Coleman is poised to become one of the elite wideouts in the country and Smothers should help as a runner and pass catcher.

Defensively, Texas must fill in some holes, especially in the back end. Having Colin Simmons, who should terrorize QBs, should help. This group has beefed up through recruiting and the portal, and DC Will Muschamp should have plenty to work with.

As expected, the schedule has plenty of teeth. A home game against Ohio State should tell us plenty, but road games at Tennessee, LSU and Texas A&M will tell us more.

The path is filled with landmines, but this Texas roster seems up for it.

This team has been on a roll, and a 10-win season in 2025 felt like a turning point. The Sun Belt is plenty competitive, especially with James Madison poised to be an issue once again. The offense will need to be rebuilt, although the defense should be solid. This is a bet on head coach Ricky Rahne, an emerging star, more than anything else.

Quarterback Blake Horvath's departure is significant. He was super for Navy over the past two seasons, and his loss is sizable. Still, Braxton Woodson has shown promise in limited action and possesses considerable ability. And the offense returns plenty of pieces around him to believe things can keep moving. This is a tricky one; there were five-plus teams worthy of real consideration.

Given the state of college football and the transfer portal, the MAC remains a sea of change. At the very least, Western Michigan will return a good chunk of its offense. The defense, which was excellent, must replace plenty. A team that won 10 of its final 11 games should contend for the conference title.

articles.title: Primer examen para Mourinho… con siete bajas y un mensaje a la cantera
articles.standfirst: Tchouaméni avanza en su recuperación, pero el técnico confirma que no jugará ante el Espanyol; tres canteranos completan la convocatoria
articles.summary: Tchouaméni avanza en su recuperación, pero el técnico confirma que no jugará ante el Espanyol; tres canteranos completan la convocatoria
articles.body: El Real Madrid ya tiene la mirada puesta en su estreno en Liga ante el Espanyol. José Mourinho dirigió este viernes la última sesión antes del debut oficial de su segunda etapa al frente del conjunto blanco, un entrenamiento en el que no pudo contar con seis futbolistas que continúan recuperándose de sus respectivas dolencias: Militao, Rodrygo, Thiago Pitarch, Mendy, Asencio y Endrick. Tchouaméni sí saltó al césped y completó trabajo con el grupo, aunque todavía no está preparado para regresar a la competición. El centrocampista francés no formará parte de la expedición madridista que viajará a Barcelona, tal y como confirmó el propio Mourinho en su comparecencia previa al encuentro. "Tchouaméni está bien, pero tiene que hacerlo todos estos días para acelerar su proceso, ya que no está para jugar contra el Espanyol", explicó el técnico portugués. El club prefiere no asumir riesgos con un jugador que está llamado a desempeñar un papel importante en los planes del entrenador esta temporada. La situación es diferente para el resto de futbolistas que permanecen en la enfermería. Militao, Rodrygo, Thiago Pitarch, Mendy, Asencio y Endrick continúan con sus respectivos trabajos de recuperación y tampoco estarán disponibles para el estreno liguero. "Obviamente que hay gente que tiene 36 entrenamientos y seis partidos; y otra que tiene cinco entrenamientos y un poco de un partido. Pero los jugadores y el staff son excepcionales. He podido preparar el trabajo diferenciado para todos, como la gente que venía aquí solo para un entrenamiento individual", aseguró. En el caso de Endrick, Mourinho desveló que el delantero brasileño arrastra "una pequeña cosa muscular", motivo por el que no podrá estar ante el Espanyol. Su ausencia se suma a una lista de bajas que reduce las alternativas del técnico para confeccionar su primera convocatoria oficial de la temporada. Mourinho tendrá que afrontar así su regreso a la competición con una plantilla todavía incompleta. "Será la primera vez que el entrenador tiene que elegir y uno juega de inicio y le sienta bien. También será la primera vez que uno vaya al banquillo y se sienta frustrado. Estos momentos son los que ellos tienen que saber digerir individualmente y como grupo", aseguró. La sesión también dejó protagonismo para la cantera. Mario Rivas, Ciria y Cestero volvieron a trabajar con el primer equipo y estarán disponibles para el partido contra el Espanyol. Mourinho confirmó que los tres jóvenes ocuparán un sitio en el banquillo en el encuentro de Barcelona. "Voy a querer también motivar a los niños y hacerles entender que la puerta está abierta. Esta semana les toca a estos tres y les tocará a muchos más. Es una cosa que me gusta hacer y que pienso que se agradece desde La Fábrica, porque es una cosa que pienso que puede motivar a los chicos”. Porteros: Courtois, Lunin y Sergio Mestre. Defensas: Huijsen, Trent, Konaté, Cucurella, Á. Carreras, Rüdiger, Dumfries y Mario Rivas. Centrocampistas: Bellingham, Camavinga, Valverde, Arda Güler, Bernardo, Cestero y Alexis Ciria. Delanteros: Vini Jr., Mbappé, C. Espí, Brahim y Yan Diomande.

articles.title: Dumfries pide paso
articles.standfirst: El lateral neerlandés, presentado oficialmente hasta 2030 en un nuevo acto privado, afronta el reto de hacerse con un puesto de peso en el nuevo Real Madrid
articles.summary: El lateral neerlandés, presentado oficialmente hasta 2030 en un nuevo acto privado, afronta el reto de hacerse con un puesto de peso en el nuevo Real Madrid
articles.body: Denzel Dumfries ya es oficialmente jugador del Real Madrid. El lateral neerlandés ha sido presentado este viernes en la Ciudad Real Madrid, donde ha firmado su contrato hasta el 30 de junio de 2030 junto a Florentino Pérez. El defensa, que lucirá el dorsal 24, afronta el reto de hacerse con un puesto de peso en el nuevo proyecto madridista. El acto se celebró en la sala de juntas de Valdebebas, con la presencia de Pirri, presidente de honor del club. Dumfries recibió una réplica del estadio, un reloj y la camiseta con su nombre antes de posar por primera vez como futbolista del Real Madrid. "Estoy muy orgulloso de jugar aquí, estoy muy agradecido y estoy deseando empezar la temporada.  Estoy muy feliz de estar aquí. Para todo el mundo es un sueño jugar en el Real Madrid. Estar aquí es una gran responsabilidad, por supuesto, porque tenemos unos objetivos importantes. Estoy muy orgulloso y muy feliz de estar aquí. Estoy listo para empezar", aseguró el lateral. Su llegada responde a una necesidad clara. Tras la salida de Dani Carvajal, el equipo necesitaba músculo, recorrido y experiencia para reforzar el lateral derecho para que Mourinho pueda tener bajo su mando dos perfiles diferentes. Dumfries reúne esas condiciones y llega a Madrid después de cinco temporadas de alto nivel en el Inter, donde disputó 207 partidos, marcó 27 goles y repartió 28 asistencias. "Es un partido muy importante. Siempre el primer partido es muy importante y por supuesto vamos a ir allí a ganar. Estoy contento de poder debutar en Liga. Deseando que llegue el partido y empezar este nuevo camino con todos. Vamos a por ello mañana". Su tarjeta de presentación en Europa también es contundente. En las semifinales de la Champions 2024/25 contra el Barcelona protagonizó una actuación memorable, con dos goles y tres asistencias. A sus 30 años, llega al Bernabéu en plena madurez futbolística y con la intención de convertir su potencia y capacidad de llegada en un argumento diferencial. El reto, sin embargo, no será sencillo. En el lateral derecho tendrá que competir con Trent, una de las grandes apuestas del club para la posición. Mourinho ya ha ensayado con ambos juntos, una posibilidad que abre la puerta a un Madrid con más alternativas y profundidad por el costado derecho.

articles.title: El Arsenal busca instaurar una nueva dinastía en la Premier 'post' Pep
articles.standfirst: Hoy arranca la Premier 26-27 • Los de Arteta arrancan con el cartel de claros favoritos para revalidar esta Premier • City, United, Chelsea, Aston Villa y Liverpool, al acecho
articles.summary: Hoy arranca la Premier 26-27 • Los de Arteta arrancan con el cartel de claros favoritos para revalidar esta Premier • City, United, Chelsea, Aston Villa y Liverpool, al acecho
articles.body: La Premier League echa a andar este viernes con el debut del vigente campeón, el Arsenal, frente al recién ascendido Coventry City de Frank Lampard. Los 'gunners' afrontan este nuevo curso habiéndose desquitado la presión de ganar un título de liga 22 años después, pero con la papeleta de claro favorito intacta. El conjunto del norte de Londres apenas ha modificado su plantel respecto al pasado curso. Y lejos de empeorar, los fichajes de Bruno Guimaraes y Tzolis suben el suelo de una de las plantillas más completas de Europa. Por detrás suya, todo es incertidumbre. El Manchester City comienza una nueva etapa sin Pep Guardiola. Enzo Maresca encabeza la renovación de un conjunto 'skyblue' que tiene la obligación de pelear por el título de liga pese a sufrir bajas cruciales en su columna vertebral. Sin Rodri ni Bernardo Silva, Elliot Anderson deberá conducir a un equipo plagado de talento en ataque, con Haaland hambriento por seguir aumentando sus registros goleadores. El Manchester United, que renació bajo la tutela de Michael Carrick y logró un meritorio tercer puesto la pasada campaña, deberá consolidar las buenas sensaciones después de un verano donde INEOS apenas se ha movido en el mercado. Tielemans y Andrey Santos llegan como recambios de Casemiro, rumbo a la MLS. Sin hacer mucho ruido, el Aston Villa de Unai Emery da un paso más a cada temporada que pasa para asaltar definitivamente el Big Six. El técnico vasco continúa sacando el máximo rendimiento a una plantilla cada vez más corta fruto de las limitaciones por el Fair Play Financiero. La venta de Rogers (138 millones) supuso una bombona de oxígeno en el excel de los ‘Villanos’. Ese dinero lo han invertido en Suzuki, Ruggeri, Manzambi, Joao Gomes y Garnacho. La zona Champions se ha convertido en el principal objetivo. El Liverpool de Iraola llega con muchas dudas a este arranque de liga. Los 'reds' encaran la era post Salah con varias incógnitas en su once: el acompañante de Van Dijk, el lateral diestro y el reemplazo del egipcio en esa banda. Xabi Alonso aterrizó en Stamford Bridge para enderezar el rumbo de un Chelsea acostumbrado a la inestabilidad deportiva e institucional en el último lustro. El tolosarra tendrá a su disposición una plantilla repleta de jóvenes talentos y con el ‘pelotazo’ de Rogers como su primer crack. Resolver su encaje junto a Palmer, la otra estrella de este Chelsea, será una de las principales misiones de Xabi al frente de los 'blues'. En un escalón inferior encontramos a la eterna incógnita del Tottenham, que con De Zerbi al frente y sus más de 250 millones de euros invertidos, debería ofrecer algo más. Ahora, es momento para que la pelota ponga a cada equipo en su sitio. La Premier está de vuelta. La Premier siempre ha tenido una relación especial con el fútbol español. Esta temporada, sin embargo, comerá en otra mesa. Prueba de ello es que habrá un total de cinco entrenadores de nuestro país en los banquillos... mientras que Lampard, Carrick y O’Neil serán los únicos ingleses. Ninguno será Guardiola, que puso fin a su brillante década en el City con seis títulos de Premier a sus espaldas. No es el único que ha hecho las maletas: Rodri ha fichado por el Barça y Nico González se queda solo. La huella de Pep, en cualquier caso, será difícil de borrar. Arteta, su alumno más aventajado, llevó al Arsenal a levantar la Premier 22 años después junto a Raya, Kepa, Mosquera, Zubimendi y Merino. También habrá morbo en el suroeste de Londres con ese 'derby' entre el Chelsea de Xabi Alonso y el Fulham de Arbeloa. Se miden, además, en la primera jornada. Los 'cotaggers', que ya contaban con Cuenca, han sumado a Palacios y Gonzalo desde La Fábrica, mientras que Chavarría llega al Bridge como reemplazo de Cucurella. Le acogerán Robert Sánchez y Marc Guiu. Iraola aterriza en Anfield con Víctor Muñoz. No nos podemos dejar a Emery y su Aston Villa campeón de Europa League con Pau Torres siendo clave, ni tampoco a un Crystal Palace ganador de Conference que ha juntado a Yeremi Pino con Mingueza. Pedro Porro seguirá en el Tottenham y Juanlu llega al Bournemouth.

articles.title: England Women's U20s World Cup squad named amid boycott threat
articles.summary: Manager Lydia Bedford has named her England squad for the upcoming Fifa U20s Women's World Cup amid ongoing threat of a boycott from European nations.
articles.body:
Manager Lydia Bedford has named her England squad for the upcoming Fifa U20s Women's World Cup amid ongoing threat of a boycott from European nations.

There have been calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign following the controversy over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

It was aborted after widespread criticism from several confederations, led by Uefa, which has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

The next upcoming Fifa tournament - therefore the first under threat of a boycott - is the U20s Women's World Cup, taking place in Poland from 5 to 27 September.

Speaking to BBC Sport after England had won a warm-up game in Portugal, Bedford spoke for the first time about the potential boycott.

"I was actually at the theatre in London when my dad rang me out of the blue and I was like 'what's happening?' From my perspective the message from leadership all along has been 'just continue as usual' so we have," she said.

"It's not something we've really even spoken to the players about because ultimately every opportunity we have to get on the grass and prepare this team we want to be in the best position possible. So all focus has been on that."

England are one of six nations from Europe taking part in the 24-team tournament alongside France, Italy, Spain, Portugal and hosts Poland.

The young Lionesses have been drawn in Group B with Brazil, Tanzania and Canada, who they face in their opening match on Saturday, 5 September (17:00 BST).

Italy, Portugal and Poland are expected to name their squads next week, while Spain announced theirs on Thursday. France have not confirmed a date.

Bedford has named a 21-player squad to represent England, which includes North Carolina Courage midfielder Erica Meg Parkinson, who received a surprise call-up to the senior squad in March.

"It's an incredibly exciting moment to name the squad and a huge achievement for every player selected," said Bedford.

"We know the level of competition in Poland will be extremely high but we're excited by the prospect of the challenge.

"For the 21 players selected, the focus now is on making the most of this opportunity, representing England with pride, and seeing how far we can go."

The top two sides from each group will automatically progress to the last 16, while the best four third-placed sides will also make it through.

The final will be hosted in Lodz on Sunday, 27 September.

articles.title: South Korea footballers urge safety after extreme heat statistics
articles.summary: South Korea professional football association urges stronger heat protections in face of rising temperatures.
articles.body:
South Korean professional footballers urged stronger protections against extreme heat ⁠after a survey by the Korea Pro-Footballers Association (KPFA) showed many players hit by dehydration, dizziness and temporary lapses in consciousness during competition.

It found 86.2% of respondents suffered significant physical strain while playing in the heat, among ⁠536 players from South Korea’s K League and WK League surveyed during a summer when pitch temperatures exceeded 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit).

Nearly two-thirds (64.7%) complained of dizziness during matches or training, while 56.6% had severe dehydration and 13% suffered lapses in consciousness.

“The fact that over 70 players experienced dizziness, dehydration, and even temporary loss of consciousness is a ‌glaring red flag,” KPFA President Lee Keun-ho, a former national team player, said in a statement.

The union called on the Korea Football Association (KFA), K League and WK League to introduce mandatory heat protocols, saying the current safeguards do not sufficiently protect players.

The KFA told the Reuters news agency that player health and safety remained its “absolute top priority” and that it fully acknowledged the concerns raised by the players’ union.

The governing body said it was taking steps to reduce heat-related risks, including adjusting match schedules and enforcing cooling-break protocols during ⁠games, while also noting some logistical challenges.

“While we face certain practical constraints, including ⁠stadium availability and tight scheduling limitations, KFA is continuously monitoring conditions to make every possible effort to prevent any heat-related incidents,” South Korea’s governing body said in a statement on Friday.

Almost half the respondents said they were dissatisfied with the current cooling-break system that usually ⁠gives players a break of just more than three minutes once temperatures reach a specified threshold.

Nearly 90% supported changes to existing match operations during extreme heat. More ⁠than half favoured later kickoff times, while others backed postponing or cancelling ⁠matches when heat advisories are in effect.

The union said women players often face additional challenges, with a number of matches scheduled during the hottest part of the day on artificial surfaces and at venues without adequate air-conditioned changing facilities.

“Playing under the scorching sun on artificial turf that ‌traps and radiates heat is essentially forcing athletes into a furnace,” KPFA Women’s President Ji So-yun said.

“Just as professional baseball proactively cancels games for the heat, football needs to stop mechanically following a rigid schedule and ‌actually ‌prioritise player health and safety.”

The KPFA said the findings should also prompt a broader discussion on South Korea’s football calendar, with many players supporting a switch to an autumn-spring schedule.

articles.title: FIFA Announces Bans, Fines Stemming from Argentina's Fight with Spain After World Cup Final
articles.summary: FIFA announced Friday that multiple players and a coach from the Argentina men's national team, plus a player from Spain's national team have been punished for their role in a post-match brawl following Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final on July 19.
articles.body:
FIFA announced Friday that multiple players and a coach from the Argentina men's national team, plus a player from Spain's national team have been punished for their role in a post-match brawl following Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final on July 19.

FIFA fined and levied a 10-match ban against Leandro Paredes, a seven-match ban against Nahuel Molina a one-match ban against Thiago Almada and a three-match ban against assistant coach Roberto Ayala, all of whom represent Argentina. Spain's Pablo Martín Gavira (Gavi) received a one-match ban as well:

Per Ben Jacobs of GiveMeSport, the Argentinian Football Association was fined $321,000, and Argentina's next two home matches in international play will see their spectator capacity limited to 50 percent:

Multiple members of the Argentine and Spanish national teams clashed after the final whistle blew for the World Cup final, including Paredes knocking both Gavi and Eric Garcia to the ground:

Tempers seemingly flared for Argentina following a disappointing performance in their attempt to become the first nation to win back-to-back World Cups since Brazil in 1958 and 1962.

Paredes, 32, was part of Argentina's World Cup-winning squad in 2022, and he currently plays his club soccer for Boca Juniors in Argentina.

Molina and Almada also won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022, and they play their club soccer for AS Roma and River Plate, respectively.

Ayala, 53, earned 116 caps for the Argentine senior national team as a center-back before transitioning into coaching and joining Argentina's staff in 2019.

Gavi, who was the only Spanish player to receive a punishment, is a 22-year-old midfielder for FC Barcelona.

In addition to winning his first World Cup title with Spain this year, Gavi is a three-time La Liga champion with Barca.

articles.title: Argentina’s Paredes gets 10-game ban for World Cup final scuffle with Spain
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes banned for 10 games as FIFA suspends three Argentina players for World Cup final scuffle with Spain.
articles.body:
FIFA banned three Argentina players, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents moments after losing the World Cup final.

The ban for Paredes, who grabbed Spain’s Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground, ranks alongside the FIFA sanctions for Uruguay forward Luis Suarez in 2014 as among the most severe in World Cup history.

Argentina defender Nahuel Molina was handed a seven-game ban while Thiago Almada was given a one-game suspension. FIFA imposed fines of $90,000 on Paredes and Molina, and $30,000 for Almada.

The ban for Paredes is effectively a one-year expulsion from the Argentina team, as the FIFA calendar for national team schedules includes 10 games through June 2027.

All of those games could be friendlies, with no competitive games currently scheduled.

Spain’s Gavi was also banned for one game, which is a Nations League match against England at Wembley on September 26.

An Argentina coach, Roberto Ayala, also got a three-game ban and a $30,000 fine.

The Argentina football federation was fined $110,000 for a range of incidents during the World Cup, including players carrying a political banner about the Falkland Islands after the semifinal win against England, and discriminatory chants by fans.

The federation was also ordered by FIFA to spend $100,000 on antiracism projects. Argentina received $34m in World Cup prize money from FIFA.

The Argentina federation can appeal the longer sanctions and fines to FIFA, and likely after, to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

In 2014, Suarez was banned from all football for four months, including for his new club Barcelona, and eight more competition games for Uruguay for biting Italy defender Giorgio Chiellini in a World Cup group-stage game in Brazil.

The on-field clashes at last month’s final — which were charged by FIFA as assault cases — came after Argentina lost a testy final to Spain where it was mostly outplayed and barely created a scoring chance.

Spain forward Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game in the second period of extra time, after Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off.

articles.body: El Arsenal quiere mantener su dominio Premier y continúa apuntalando su plantilla para afrontar una nueva temporada en la que volverá a tener grandes objetivos. Los 'gunners' de Mikel Arteta han cerrado el fichaje de Ezri Konsa, que llega procedente del Aston Villa por 51 millones de libras. El central inglés llegó al conjunto 'villano' en la temporada 2019-20 procedente del Brentford y, temporada tras temporada, se consolidó como una pieza indiscutible en la zaga del Villa. También lo ha sido bajo las órdenes de Unai Emery, quien ha confiado en él como uno de los pilares de su defensa. Mundialista con los 'Three Lions' en la última cita veraniega, se convierte en una nueva pieza para reforzar el entramado defensivo del conjunto londinense. Acostumbrado a desenvolverse en el sector derecho de la zaga, tanto como central como, de manera puntual, en el lateral, se incorpora a una línea defensiva de primer nivel junto a nombres como Jurriën Timber, Cristhian Mosquera y Ben White. Su llegada también responde a las necesidades defensivas que arrastra el Arsenal tras la lesión de espalda de William Saliba y los problemas físicos que arrastra Timber. El ex del Aston Villa se convierte en la cuarta incorporación para el técnico vasco en este mercado estival, que poco a poco va dando forma a una plantilla de ensueño. articles.title: El Shakhtar Donetsk jugará de local en Stamford Bridge en la Champions
articles.standfirst: El club ucraniano lo ha hecho oficial por sus canales oficiales
articles.summary: El club ucraniano lo ha hecho oficial por sus canales oficiales
articles.body: Stamford Bridge será estadio de Champions League en la temporada 26/27, pero no será por el Chelsea. El Shakthar Donetsk ha anunciado que el estadio inglés será su sede para la disputa del torneo europeo durante toda esta campaña. "Jugar nuestros partidos de Champions League como local en Stamford Bridge es una oportunidad especial para el Shakhtar. Estamos agradecidos al Chelsea Football Club por la oportunidad de albergar nuestros partidos en este lugar tan especial", reza el comunicado del club. Ambas directivas se han puesto de acuerdo para esta medida que no es novedosa para el Shakhtar Donetsk. Debido a su situación geopolítica, el club ucraniano ha jugado sus encuentros de Champions como local en diferentes sedes europeas como Alemania, Polonia o Eslovenia. Ahora probará fortuna en el estadio de un club con el que guarda buena relación. El Chelsea ha sido partícipe de la venta más cara de la historia del club ucraniano. Desembolsó alrededor de 70 millones de euros por Mudryk, un jugador que volverá a jugar, después de que le levantaran su suspensión por dopaje. Willian Borges ha sido otro de los que ha pasado por las filas de ambos equipos.  Cuatro años después de que el empresario ruso Roman Abramovich vendiera el Chelsea y que todos los beneficios fueran donados a las víctimas de la guerra en Ucrania, un equipo de este país jugará en Stamford Bridge como local para disputar la Champions. El Chelsea ha emitido este anuncio por sus redes sociales. "Tras la decepcionante temporada 2025/26 del Chelsea FC y su fracaso en la clasificación para competiciones europeas, el club se complace en brindar al FC Shakhtar la oportunidad de jugar en Londres, la capital del Reino Unido, en su campaña de la Liga de Campeones", reza el comunicado.

articles.title: A Maresca le entran las prisas tras la salida de Rodri
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico del Manchester City espera poder realizar nuevas incorporaciones en esta recta final de mercado
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico del Manchester City espera poder realizar nuevas incorporaciones en esta recta final de mercado
articles.body: El próximo domingo, Enzo Maresca se presentará ante el Etihad Stadium en el primer partido de la Premier League 26-27 contra el Bournemouth. A la par, el club sigue trabajando en el mercado... y al técnico italiano le están entrando las prisas. "No estoy preocupado ni inquieto por lo que está sucediendo en estas últimas semanas. Desde el primer día, sabíamos exactamente lo que necesitábamos y estamos trabajando juntos con Hugo Viana (director deportivo) y el resto del club", arrancó diciendo un Enzo Maresca que apuntó que "muchas cosas pueden suceder" en estos 10 últimos días de mercado. La idea de contratar a Maresca como sucesor de Guardiola venía a reflejar la línea continuista del proyecto. Pero, a la hora de operar en el mercado, no todo parece estar yendo sobre raíles. Y es que, a pesar de anticiparse al convertir a Elliot Anderson en el fichaje más caro de su historia, el Manchester City apenas lo ha complementado con Monga y Rulli... mientras que ha dejado salir a Rodri, Bernardo, Trafford, Aké y Stones. "Como he dicho varias veces, si hay jugadores que se van... otros tienen que llegar", explicaba Maresca, quien también recalcó su imposibilidad por retener a Rodri Hernández. "Quería marcharse". Aprovechó, también, para confirmar prácticamente la salida de Savinho al Tottenham. "Quería irse desde el primer día". No será el último, ya que Marmosuh también se acerca a los 'spurs'. "Veremos qué pasa". Lógicamente, cómo le sucedió ayer a Xabi Alonso, el de Enzo Fernández fue uno de los nombres que salieron a la palestra en la rueda de prensa. "Es un jugador del Chelsea, y no voy a hablar de jugadores que no están con nosotros. En primer lugar, porque creo que es una falta de respeto, y en segundo lugar porque no me gusta cuando diferentes entrenadores hablan de nuestros jugadores". La abultada derrota en la Community Shield contra el Arsenal supuso un primer aviso. "Somos un club que no puede esperar para competir. Necesitamos hacerlo desde el primer día". No tiene dudas de que van "a ganar partidos". Pero espera que Hugo Viana tape todos los agujeros que se le han abierto al Manchester City en esta recta final de mercado.

articles.title: Arsenal vs. Coventry City Live Premier League Matchweek 1 Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: WHAT TO KNOW
articles.body:
Amid a backdrop of "Championes" chants at the Emirates Stadium, Premier League title holders Arsenal got the 2026-27 season underway with a confident, straightforward win against newly promoted Coventry City.

Kai Havertz got the opening goal of the campaign, coolly guiding home Riccardo Calafiori's pass to give the Gunners a deserved lead in the 15th minute.

Bukayo Saka got in on the fun 10 minutes later, tapping home from yards out with the goal at his mercy following good work from Declan Rice and Christos Tzolis.

The champions went into the half with a comfortable 2-0 lead, holding 67% possession and restricting the Sky Blues to just two shots, neither of which was on target.

In an early contender for the weirdest goal of the season, Martin Ødegaard made it three just minutes after the restart. The Norwegian completely scuffed his kick when Ben White's pass met him outside the six-yard box, but the ball bobbled awkwardly towards Carl Rushworth's goal, and there was little the keeper could do to keep it out.

With the game all but won, the Gunners took their foot off the gas for the remainder of the second half, but they remained far superior to a Coventry side that will need a lot more to survive another season in the Premier League.

It was a baptism of fire for Coventry in their first Premier League game for 25 years, but with fellow promoted club Hull City up next, they have a real chance to grab what could already be a vital three points.

Arsenal, meanwhile, will look to keep up the momentum on the road against Aston Villa. With an effortless 3-0 win, the Gunners have already put the league on notice.

articles.title: Miguel Ángel Gil: "Vamos a ayudar a Julián, le necesitamos para competir entre los grandes"
articles.standfirst: El CEO del Atlético zanja definitivamente la posible salida del argentino
articles.summary: El CEO del Atlético zanja definitivamente la posible salida del argentino
articles.body: Se terminó el culebrón Julián Alvarez, si es que no estaba cerrado desde hace meses. Miguel Ángel Gil, CEO del Atlético, ha zanjado definitivamente la posible salida del delantero argentino con unas declaraciones a la Agencia EFE. La Araña ha sido uno de los nombres del verano. El futbolista que más espacio ha ocupado en las tertulias de radio, en los programas de televisión, en las webs deportivas y en las páginas de los periódicos. Se acabó. La Araña seguirá vistiendo la camiseta del Atlético. El consejero delegado del Atlético de Madrid insistió este viernes a EFE en la continuidad de Julián Alvarez en el equipo y remarcó que el club rojiblanco va a "ayudar" al atacante y lo va a "seguir cuidando" para que dé "todo su potencial" y remarcó que le necesitan "para seguir compitiendo entre los grandes de Europa". Miguel Ángel Gil quiso zanjar una vez más el debate sobre el futuro de Julián. El CEO del club ya había hablado sobre este asunto de manera muy contundente el pasado 17 de julio. Un mes después vuelve a confirmar lo dicho en aquel momento. "El Atlético de Madrid, como todos los grandes clubes, se construye con grandes jugadores y tengo claro que Julián lo es, además de un gran profesional. Debemos competir con nuestros valores, con gente de la casa y con los mejores jugadores de fuera que podamos incorporar", aseguró. Tras meses con la situación del futbolista en boca de todos, Miguel Ángel se refirió al futuro inmediato del jugador y el rol del Atlético.  "Vamos a ayudar a Julián y le vamos a seguir cuidando para que pueda darnos todo su potencial, porque le necesitamos para seguir compitiendo entre los grandes de Europa. Debemos comprender que Julián no ha tenido cerca a los mejores consejeros sobre su carrera profesional en los últimos meses", advirtió. Y añadió además un mensaje claro para el FC Barcelona. "No podemos permitir que otros clubes y sus medios afines decidan lo que tenemos que hacer, marquen nuestra estrategia deportiva y nos falten al respeto".  "Eso es precisamente lo que buscan: dividirnos. Está claro que no somos tan poderosos como ellos, pero nosotros tenemos valores. Los atléticos no vamos a permitir que nos contaminen. El Atleti es fuerte cuando estamos todos juntos", recalcó Miguel Ángel Gil. El Atlético de Madrid ha sido muy claro con la situación de Julián desde hace meses. El club rojiblanco mantiene la misma postura inicial y no tiene intención de traspasar al futbolista argentino que sigue trabajando con normalidad a las órdenes del Cholo y podría ser convocado para medirse al Villarreal el próximo domingo. Desde el club se remiten a su cláusula y su contrato descartar cualquier salida, ya sea rumbo a Barcelona o al Arsenal. Para el Atlético no hay más debate, Julián se queda en el cuadro rojiblanco.

articles.title: Usain Bolt: Olympics icon registers to play for Manchester Sunday league team
articles.summary: Eight-time Olympic champion sprinter Usain Bolt has registered to play for a veterans' Sunday league football team in Manchester.
articles.body:
Eight-time Olympic champion sprinter Usain Bolt has registered to play for a veterans' Sunday league football team in Manchester.

The Football Association's Full-Time website has the 40-year-old Jamaican as a registered player for Wythenshawe Vets FC, who play in the Premier Division of the Cheshire Veterans Football League.

The over-35s team based in south Manchester attracted attention last year for assembling a squad full of former Premier League players .

Wythenshawe's squad for this season includes former professionals such as England and Liverpool striker Emile Heskey, Everton striker Oumar Niasse, Manchester United captain Antonio Valencia, Newcastle striker Papiss Cisse, Manchester City duo Stephen Ireland and Nedum Onuoha and Premier League title winners Joleon Lescott and Danny Drinkwater.

Bolt is the fastest man in history over 100m and 200m, having set the world records for both distances at the 2009 Athletics World Championships.

After retiring from athletics in 2017, he pursued a career in professional football.

In 2018 Bolt scored twice in a friendly for Australian A-League side Central Coast Mariners, and signed a contract with the club after rejecting a two-year offer from Maltese side Valletta, but left just eight weeks later.

Wythenshawe, who have not officially announced Bolt's registration, have been contacted for comment.

articles.body: El RCDE Stadium es el escenario en el que echa a andar el nuevo Madrid, el de Jose Mourinho. Ante un equipo que arrancó la temporada de manera exuberante con su 3-0 al Levante, el conjunto blanco presenta sus armas para recuperar un título que en las dos últimas temporadas fue a parar a las vitrinas del Barcelona El cuadro perico se presenta con las pilas cargadas después del excelente estreno que brindó a su afición. Lo hace con las ausencias de Cabrera, que cumple el segundo de los tres partidos de sanción que recibió por golpear la pantalla del VAR la temporada pasada, en el encuentro ante el Getafe correspondiente a la jornada 29. Los distintos recursos presentados aplazaron el cumplimiento de la sanción hasta el inicio de esta temporada. Además, el equipo cuenta con las bajas por lesión de Javi Puado y Kike García. En el lado del Real Madrid, son siete las ausencias para este estreno liguero, todas ellas por problemas físicos: Mendy, Asencio, Militão, Tchouaméni, Thiago Pitarch, Rodrygo y Endrick. Esta situación obliga a Mourinho a recurrir a tres canteranos para completar la convocatoria: Mario Rivas, Cestero y Alexis Ciria. Onces confirmados: Espanyol: Dmitrovic; El Hilali, Riedel, Unai Núlez, Hinojo; Urko, Edu Expósito; Calatrava, Javier Hernández, Dolan; Roberto. Real Madrid: Coutois; Dumfries, Konaté, Huijsen, Carreras; Valverde, Bernardo Silva; Güler, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappé.

articles.title: Nick Saban Says Alabama 'Could Sneak Up on People' in 2026, Hypes Georgia, Texas for CFP Runs
articles.summary: Legendary former Alabama head coach Nick Saban believes that the Crimson Tide can exceed expectations during the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Legendary former Alabama head coach Nick Saban believes that the Crimson Tide can exceed expectations during the 2026 college football season.

Saban said that Alabama was "under-the-radar" and "may be able to sneak up on people" during a Friday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:47 mark).

He also discussed the College Football Playoff outlook for Georgia and head coach Kirby Smart as well as Texas and head coach Steve Sarkisian.

"I talked to Kirby and Sark both and I think both of those guys have really, really good teams," Saban said (0:27 mark). "I think they're probably the two teams that, at least on paper looking at this season, probably have the best chance to be successful and maybe go a long way in the playoff."

Alabama is coming off a CFP quarterfinal appearance last season, finishing with an 11-4 record under head coach Kalen DeBoer.

The Crimson Tide still boast one of the country's top secondaries, owning the SEC's No. 1 pass defense in 2025 by allowing a mere 169.9 yards per game through the air.

While quarterback Ty Simpson is no longer in the mix after he was selected in the 2026 NFL draft, Keelon Russell and Austin Mack are battling to start under center for Alabama.

Georgia is attempting to clinch a third consecutive CFP berth this year after ranking No. 3 in the preseason Associated Press Top 25 .

Although there's some uncertainty surrounding the Bulldogs' receiving corps following the departures of Zachariah Branch and Colbie Young, Smart's squad still contains plenty of talent.

Texas closed its 2025 campaign on a high note and finished at 10-3, but missed the CFP.

The Longhorns are once again led by Arch Manning at quarterback and brought in a transfer portal class that ranked No. 3 in the country, per 247Sports .

Texas sat at No. 5 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll.
